note: Both sets share the same core claims about the sub-panel, inverters, NFDS units and junction box, and both repeat the 3-wire and NEMA 3R facts under two names and both misbind 'ground fault' to the Main Breaker when the note attributes it to the inverter's ground fault protection device. Set A additionally captures the substantive note-4 content (ground fault protection required per the NEC 690.42 exception), which Set B only reduces to a vague 'compliance' claim, but A also misreads the label 20 as a wire size and invents a 20→34 connection. Set B's extras are almost entirely trivia (labels 20 and 34, 'terminal value' claims), one of which misplaces the value 4 at the lower terminal when 31 is the lower label. On balance A carries the more important engineering fact despite its two bad claims.
remarks: The circled numbers 20/31/4/34/5 are diagram reference or terminal labels, not wire sizes or ratings; both extractions try to turn them into engineering values. Both sets also state the 3-wire configuration three times (PV Equipment wire configuration, PV Equipment wire count, SUB-PANEL PV wire count) and the NEMA 3R sub-panel enclosure twice. The note-4 fact that the required conductor-to-ground bond is made by the ground fault protection device is only weakly represented in either set.
